headline_marked: [[Application deadline for 1,460 meter reader jobs]] in Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board nears
headline: Application deadline for 1,460 meter reader jobs in Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board nears
summary: The application window for 1,460 Meter Reader cum Messenger positions under the Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board closes on July 21, 2026. Candidates need an SSC or equivalent degree and a personal bicycle.
details: The application period for 1,460 Meter Reader cum Messenger positions under the Bangladesh Rural Electrification Board (BREB) is closing soon. Interested candidates have until 5 PM on July 21, 2026, to apply online.

These contract-based roles are primarily field-oriented. Employees will be responsible for collecting electricity meter readings from customers in designated areas and accurately recording them for billing.
Key duties also include identifying faulty meters, broken seals, or illegal connections and reporting them to the authorities. This ensures accurate bill preparation for consumers.

Applicants must have passed SSC or an equivalent examination and possess strong basic arithmetic skills (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division). Good handwriting is also a mandatory requirement.

Candidates must be honest, trustworthy, of good character, and have a pleasant personality with a robust physique. A willingness to travel to remote rural areas for meter reading and bill distribution is essential, along with owning a personal bicycle.

Selected candidates will need to deposit BDT 10,000 as a security bond at the Palli Bidyut Samity's cash branch upon joining. Those who applied properly for the advertisement published on May 14, 2025, do not need to reapply.

headline_marked: [[Teenager escapes pirates, survives three days alone]] in Sundarbans before returning home
headline: Teenager escapes pirates, survives three days alone in Sundarbans before returning home
summary: A 16-year-old boy, kidnapped by pirates while crab fishing in the Sundarbans, managed to escape his captors and spent three harrowing days alone in the dense forest before finding his way back to his village. His community had launched a massive search operati
details: A 16-year-old boy, Mehedi Hasan, has returned home to Koyra, Khulna, after a harrowing six-day ordeal. He escaped from pirate captivity and then spent three days and nights alone in the dense Sundarbans forest before finding his way back to civilization.

Mehedi had gone crab fishing in the Sundarbans' Jolakali canal with other forest dwellers, defying a ban on entry during the breeding season. Their boat was ambushed by the 'Afzal Bahini' pirate group, led by Afzal Hossain.
The pirates abducted Mehedi, demanding a ransom of BDT 25,000 from his family for his release. His family arranged the money, but Mehedi managed to escape before the payment could be delivered.

After fleeing the pirate boat, Mehedi spent three terrifying days navigating the deep jungle, constantly fearing recapture. He ran like a deer chased by a tiger, even avoiding his own family's search boats, mistaking them for pirates.
He endured beatings from the pirates and had nothing to eat during his time in the forest. Upon his return, he was found with bruises and swollen feet, exhausted from the ordeal.

His family and over 150 villagers had launched a massive search operation, scouring the rivers and canals of the Sundarbans, calling out his name with megaphones. News of his return brought immense relief to the community.
Mehedi was eventually found in the Uttar Bedkashi Union area and reunited with his family. A general diary had been filed with the police regarding his disappearance.

According to Mehedi's uncle, the 'Afzal Bahini' is now led by Afzal Hossain, who took over after their previous leader was arrested by the Coast Guard. Forest department officials noted that Mehedi had entered the Sundarbans illegally.
